 All BREAKING NEWS 3 Nov 15, 2026, 08:54 GMT+0 Iranian lawmaker warns of response if US launches nuclear attack
 An Iranian lawmaker warned Sunday that Tehran would demonstrate what he called “absolute deterrence” if the United States launched a nuclear attack on parts of Iran.
 Ahmad Rastineh, spokesman for parliament’s defense and national power faction, said Iran was approaching “absolute deterrence” through the work of its nuclear scientists and could display that capability in response to what he called a US miscalculation involving unconventional weapons.
 “If there is a US miscalculation in launching a nuclear attack on some areas of the country, we will demonstrate this absolute deterrence so extensively that the world will be astonished by its power,” he said.
 He also said uranium enrichment was among the least advanced of Iran’s nuclear technologies, and claimed Israeli and Pakistani nuclear technology was “very insignificant and inferior” compared with Iran’s.
 100 % Nov 15, 2026, 08:39 GMT+0 BREAKING NEWS Bahrain condemns Iran's attacks as violation of sovereignty
 Bahrain condemned on Sunday continuing Iranian attacks on the country, describing them as a violation of its sovereignty and a threat to regional security.
 The Foreign Ministry said Bahrain’s air defenses intercepted and destroyed drones on Sunday, and two more on Friday and said Iran’s Revolutionary Guards had explicitly claimed responsibility for the attacks.
 “These attacks constitute a blatant aggression against Bahrain’s sovereignty and territorial integrity,” the ministry said.
 It also called them a “flagrant violation” of UN Security Council Resolution 2817, which condemned Iranian attacks on Bahrain and neighboring countries and demanded they stop.
 The ministry said the attacks targeted the safety of residents and undermined efforts to ease tensions.
 It rejected Iran’s justifications, saying no excuse could justify violating another country’s sovereignty or territorial integrity.
 Bahrain held Iran fully responsible for the attacks and their consequences, and said it reserved the right to individual and collective self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter.
 The ministry urged the Security Council to condemn the attacks and take firm action to ensure Iran complies with the resolution.
 Nov 15, 2026, 08:20 GMT+0 BREAKING NEWS Iran says it will keep responding to attacks after reported Bahrain strikes
 Iran will continue responding to attacks, the Foreign Ministry spokesman said Sunday, in response to a question about reports of recent attacks on Bahrain.
 “We have previously said that we will not leave any attack unanswered, and we will continue this approach from now on,” Esmail Baghaei said at a news conference.
 He said there was no meaningful difference among US officials over the war with Iran and that decisions were made “somewhere else,” not in Washington.
 He added that using diplomacy did not mean placing hope in any party. “American diplomats have their daggers drawn,” he said.
 Iran would accept no commitments regarding its nuclear program and was not currently in a position to do so, Baghaei added.
 100 % Nov 15, 2026, 07:56 GMT+0 Iran says it will seek reparations from regional countries
 Iran will pursue reparations from regional countries, the Foreign Ministry spokesman said Sunday, dismissing as baseless a compensation demand made by the Gulf Cooperation Council’s secretary-general.
 Esmail Baghaei said Iran’s military actions were not directed against neighboring countries but were defensive measures against the origins of attacks on Iran, under Article 51 of the UN Charter.
 He also accused countries in the region of assisting attacks on Iran by making their airspace, waters and territory available to its enemies, adding that Tehran had documented their role.
 He said some regional countries had also provided Iraq with aid during the Iran–Iraq War.

 Nov 15, 2026, 07:24 GMT+0 BREAKING NEWS Bahrain says air defenses destroy several Iranian aerial attacks
 Bahrain’s air defenses intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks on Sunday before they reached their targets, the Bahrain Defense Force said.
 The force accused Iran of continuing a “systematic hostile approach” against the country and said its units remained on high alert to defend the country. 
 Nov 15, 2026, 06:37 GMT+0 Iran’s parliament speaker urges officials to stop repeated comments on gasoline policy
 Iranian officials should avoid making repeated public statements about gasoline policy because they are worrying people, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Sunday. 
 “Gasoline and the energy imbalance are technical and national issues that can be resolved through collective wisdom, expert analysis, sound decisions and public cooperation,” he said in remarks to parliament.
 Ghalibaf added that any decision should be made with public support and in a way that places the least burden on people. Officials responsible for the issue should understand its sensitivity and importance, he said, and “strictly avoid repeated positions and comments.”
 100 % Nov 15, 2026, 06:34 GMT+0 MPs approve fast-track review of proposal on intelligence minister
 Iran’s parliament voted Sunday to expedite consideration of a bill that would remove the requirement that the country's intelligence minister be qualified in Islamic jurisprudence (ijtihad).
 The motion received 192 votes in favor, 49 against and four abstentions among 247 lawmakers present.
 The proposal had initially been scheduled for a two-urgency vote. Ebrahim Azizi, head of parliament’s national security committee, proposed a single-urgency vote to allow time for expert review.
 Nov 15, 2026, 05:57 GMT+0 Ghalibaf says Iran will not remain in ‘neither war nor peace’ state
 Iran will not remain in a state of “neither war nor peace,” Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Sunday.
 Ghalibaf said Tehran did not care whether Washington wanted negotiations or war, but added that a path to an agreement would open if the United States accepted Iran’s seven conditions. 
 “If the Americans make a mistake this time, the geography of the battle will be determined by the capabilities and will of our armed forces,” he said.
 He also described the unveiling of an underground missile city during the war as a valuable achievement and a sign of changing strategic equations in the region.
 100 % Nov 15, 2026, 05:40 GMT+0 US says Basij chief cannot preach human rights while Iran represses protesters
 The US State Department accused Basij paramilitary chief Hossein Taeb of hypocrisy on human rights after he appeared at a film festival in Tehran and spoke about non-interference while Iran violently suppresses peaceful protests.
 In a post on its Persian-language account, USABehFarsi, the department said, Taeb had spoken about non-interference before an international audience while praising bloodshed carried out by the Iranian government.
 “Defending vulnerable people while peaceful protests at home are violently suppressed requires astonishing audacity,” the post said.
 It said Iranian security forces had shot thousands of young protesters over the past decade, adding that the government’s response had been “silence, arrests and denial.”
 It also said film festivals and selected poetry could not “whitewash this simple truth: a government that kills its own citizens to stay in power has no standing to lecture others.” 
 Nov 15, 2026, 04:15 GMT+0 Iran's IRGC says six drones targeted US radar site in Bahrain
 Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said in a statement they targeted a US air-defense radar at Bahrain’s Al Riffa helicopter base with six drones, describing the attack as a second round of retaliation for US military action.
 The United States has not responded to the allegation yet.
 The Guards said their Aerospace Force carried out the operation and claimed the drones struck their target.
 The force also claimed the Strait of Hormuz remained closed and threatened a stronger response to any further US attacks.
 It accused Washington of using naval escort operations as cover for “oil smuggling” through the strait and carrying out attacks to divert attention from what it described as the failure of those operations.
 The Guards also claimed American drones were being shot down and said they had deployed more drones against US targets in this round than in the previous one.
